purpose: Teach: 蛍光/ボーイ/ソナタ/ネズミ/愛好/コメディ/明快/大作

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、寝るとき、蛍光時計、よく見たな、楽しかった。
lines.en: When I was young, I used to watch the luminous clock before sleep. It was such a joy.
lines.style: Slow, gentle opening. Distant gaze—eyes following memory. Warm and unhurried, like turning pages of something beloved. Soft landing on the final word.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。新婚旅行のボーイさん、優しかったわね、覚えてる?
lines.en: Yes. That kind bellboy on our honeymoon—do you remember him?
lines.style: Soft affirmation. Slight lift in the middle on the memory itself. Searching tone, inviting him to remember with her. Intimate, no distance between them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: モーツァルトのソナタ、好きだったな、お祖父ちゃん、聴いてた。
lines.en: I loved Mozart's sonatas. My grandfather used to listen to them.
lines.style: Gentle pause before the memory surfaces. Reverent on the composer's name. Quieter on the final clause—respect mixed with longing. The voice of someone honoring what shaped him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の田舎の家、ネズミ、よく出てきたわね、夜。
lines.en: Mice used to come through that old country house at night, didn't they?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact beginning. A small laugh underneath—not complaining, remembering. The tone of someone who has made peace with small troubles. Trails off gently, inviting recognition.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、私、書道愛好家として、活動していたよ。
lines.en: When I was young, I was quite active as a calligraphy enthusiast.
lines.style: Quiet pride without boasting. Steady pace. The particular care of someone speaking about a discipline they loved. Slight emphasis on the commitment—not a hobby, but a practice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お正月のコメディ番組、笑ったわね、二人で。
lines.en: We laughed so hard at those New Year's comedy programs, remember?
lines.style: Brightness surfaces—the shared laughter lives in the voice. Warm and conspiratorial. A little lift on the memory. The affection of two people who know each other's laugh.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の本、明快な文体で、読みやすかったな、明治の。
lines.en: Those old books from the Meiji era—the prose was so clear and easy to read.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost professorial tone. Appreciation for craftsmanship in the voice. Slow enough to let the listener feel the satisfaction of well-made sentences. Contented exhale at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 晩年の作家、大作を残した方、多いわね、文学界に。
lines.en: So many late-career writers left behind their masterpieces, didn't they? The literary world was full of them.
lines.style: Observational and steady. A note of reverence for achievement and legacy. Slight pause before the final thought, as if cataloging a truth. Trails off with quiet satisfaction—she's witnessed something worth witnessing.
